{{Short description|Mathematical concept}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Maurer&ndash;Cartan form''' for a [[Lie group]] {{math|''G''}} is a distinguished [[differential form|differential one-form]] on {{math|''G''}} that carries the basic [[infinitesimal]] information about the structure of {{math|''G''}}. It was much used by [[Élie Cartan]] as a basic ingredient of his [[method of moving frames]], and bears his name together with that of [[Ludwig Maurer]].

As a one-form, the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form is peculiar in that it takes its values in the [[Lie algebra]] associated to the Lie group {{math|''G''}}.  The Lie algebra is identified with the [[tangent space]] of {{math|''G''}} at the identity, denoted {{math|T<sub>''e''</sub>''G''}}.  The Maurer&ndash;Cartan form {{math|''ω''}} is thus a one-form defined globally on {{math|''G''}}, that is, a linear mapping of the tangent space {{math|T<sub>''g''</sub>''G''}} at each {{math|''g'' ∈ ''G''}} into {{math|T<sub>''e''</sub>''G''}}.  It is given as the [[pushforward (differential)|pushforward]] of a vector in {{math|T<sub>''g''</sub>''G''}} along the left-translation in the group:
:<math>\omega(v) = (L_{g^{-1}})_* v,\quad v\in T_gG.</math>

==Motivation and interpretation==
{{see also|Lie group action}}
A Lie group acts on itself by multiplication under the mapping
:<math>G\times G \ni (g,h) \mapsto gh \in G.</math>
A question of importance to Cartan and his contemporaries was how to identify a [[principal homogeneous space]] of {{math|''G''}}. That is, a [[manifold]] {{math|''P''}} identical to the group {{math|''G''}}, but without a fixed choice of unit element.  This motivation came, in part, from [[Felix Klein]]'s [[Erlangen programme]] where one was interested in a notion of [[symmetry]] on a space, where the symmetries of the space were [[transformation group|transformation]]s forming a Lie group.  The geometries of interest were [[homogeneous space]]s {{math|''G''/''H''}}, but usually without a fixed choice of origin corresponding to the [[coset]] {{math|''eH''}}.

A principal homogeneous space of {{math|''G''}} is a manifold {{math|''P''}} abstractly characterized by having a [[Group action (mathematics)|free and transitive action]] of {{math|''G''}} on {{math|''P''}}.  The '''Maurer&ndash;Cartan form'''<ref>Introduced by Cartan (1904).</ref> gives an appropriate ''infinitesimal'' characterization of the principal homogeneous space.  It is a one-form defined on {{math|''P''}} satisfying an [[integrability condition]] known as the Maurer&ndash;Cartan equation.  Using this integrability condition, it is possible to define the [[exponential map (Lie theory)|exponential map]] of the Lie algebra and in this way obtain, locally, a group action on {{math|''P''}}.

==Construction==

===Intrinsic construction===
Let {{math|'''g''' ≅ T<sub>''e''</sub>''G''}} be the tangent space of a Lie group {{math|''G''}} at the identity (its [[Lie algebra]]). {{math|''G''}} acts on itself by left translation
:<math> L : G \times G \to G</math>
such that for a given {{math|''g'' ∈ ''G''}} we have

:<math> L_g : G \to G \quad \mbox{where} \quad L_g(h) = gh,</math>

and this induces a map of the [[tangent bundle]] to itself:
<math>(L_g)_*:T_hG\to T_{gh}G.</math>
A left-invariant [[vector field]] is a section {{math|''X''}} of {{math|T''G''}} such that <ref>Subtlety: <math>(L_g)_{*}X </math> gives a vector in <math> T_{gh}G \text{ if } X\in T_h G</math></ref>

:<math>(L_g)_{*}X = X \quad \forall g \in G.</math>

The '''Maurer&ndash;Cartan form''' {{math|''ω''}} is a {{math|'''g'''}}-valued one-form on {{math|''G''}} defined on vectors {{math|''v'' ∈ T<sub>''g''</sub>''G''}} by the formula

: <math>\omega_g(v)=(L_{g^{-1}})_*v.</math>

===Extrinsic construction===
{{Rewrite section|date=June 2026}}
If {{math|''G''}} is embedded in {{math|GL(''n'')}} by a matrix valued mapping {{math|''g'' {{=}}(''g''<sub>''ij''</sub>)}}, then one can write {{math|''ω''}} explicitly as

:<math>\omega_g = g^{-1} \,dg.</math>

In this sense, the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form is always the left [[logarithmic derivative]] of the [[Identity function|identity map]] of {{math|''G''}}.

===Characterization as a connection===
If we regard the Lie group {{math|''G''}} as a [[principal bundle]] over a manifold consisting of a single point then the Maurer–Cartan form can also be characterized abstractly as the unique [[connection (principal bundle)|principal connection]] on the principal bundle {{math|''G''}}. Indeed, it is the unique {{math|'''g''' {{=}} T<sub>''e''</sub>''G''}} valued {{math|1}}-form on {{math|''G''}} satisfying

:# <math>\omega_e = \mathrm{id} : T_eG\rightarrow {\mathfrak g},\text{ and}</math>
:# <math>\forall g \in G \quad \omega_g = \mathrm{Ad}(h)(R_h^*\omega_e),\text{ where }h=g^{-1},</math>

where {{math|''R''<sub>''h''</sub>*}} is the [[pullback (differential geometry)|pullback]] of forms along the right-translation in the group and {{math|Ad(''h'')}} is the [[adjoint representation of a Lie group|adjoint action]] on the Lie algebra.

==Properties==
If {{math|''X''}} is a left-invariant vector field on {{math|''G''}}, then {{math|''ω''(''X'')}} is constant on {{math|''G''}}. Furthermore, if {{math|''X''}} and {{math|''Y''}} are both left-invariant, then

:<math>\omega([X,Y])=[\omega(X),\omega(Y)]</math>

where the bracket on the left-hand side is the [[Lie bracket of vector fields]], and the bracket on the right-hand side is the bracket on the Lie algebra {{math|'''g'''}}.  (This may be used as the definition of the bracket on {{math|'''g'''}}.)  These facts may be used to establish an isomorphism of Lie algebras

:<math>\mathfrak{g}=T_eG\cong \{\hbox{left-invariant vector fields on G}\}.</math>

By the definition of the [[exterior derivative]], if {{math|''X''}} and {{math|''Y''}} are arbitrary vector fields then

:<math>d\omega(X,Y)=X(\omega(Y))-Y(\omega(X))-\omega([X,Y]).</math>

Here {{math|''ω''(''Y'')}} is the {{math|'''g'''}}-valued function obtained by duality from pairing the one-form {{math|''ω''}} with the vector field {{math|''Y''}}, and {{math|''X''(''ω''(''Y''))}} is the [[Lie derivative]] of this function along {{math|''X''}}. Similarly {{math|''Y''(''ω''(''X''))}} is the Lie derivative along {{math|''Y''}} of the {{math|'''g'''}}-valued function {{math|''ω''(''X'')}}.

In particular, if {{math|''X''}} and {{math|''Y''}} are left-invariant, then

:<math>X(\omega(Y))=Y(\omega(X))=0,</math>

so

:<math>d\omega(X,Y)+[\omega(X),\omega(Y)]=0</math>

but the left-invariant fields span the tangent space at any point (the push-forward of a basis in {{math|T<sub>''e''</sub>''G''}} under a diffeomorphism is still a basis), so the equation is true for any pair of vector fields {{math|''X''}} and {{math|''Y''}}.  This is known as the '''Maurer&ndash;Cartan equation'''.  It is often written as

:<math>d\omega + \frac{1}{2}[\omega,\omega]=0.</math>

Here {{math|[ω, ω]}} denotes the [[bracket of Lie algebra-valued forms]].

==Maurer&ndash;Cartan frame==
One can also view the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form as being constructed from a '''Maurer&ndash;Cartan frame'''.  Let {{math|''E''<sub>i</sub>}} be a [[vector space basis|basis]] of sections of {{math|T''G''}} consisting of left-invariant vector fields, and {{math|''θ''<sup>''j''</sup>}} be the [[dual basis]] of sections of {{math|T<sup>*</sup>''G''}} such that {{math|''θ''<sup>''j''</sup>(''E''<sub>''i''</sub>) {{=}} ''δ''<sub>''i''</sub><sup>''j''</sup>}}, the [[Kronecker delta]].  Then {{math|''E''<sub>''i''</sub>}} is a Maurer&ndash;Cartan frame, and {{math|''θ''<sup>''i''</sup>}} is a '''Maurer&ndash;Cartan coframe'''.

Since {{math|''E''<sub>''i''</sub>}} is left-invariant, applying the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form to it simply returns the value of {{math|''E''<sub>''i''</sub>}} at the identity. Thus {{math|''ω''(''E''<sub>''i''</sub>) {{=}} ''E''<sub>''i''</sub>(''e'') ∈ '''g'''}}.  Thus, the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form can be written
{{NumBlk|:|<math>\omega=\sum_iE_i(e)\otimes\theta^i.</math>|{{EquationRef|1}}}}

Suppose that the Lie brackets of the vector fields {{math|''E''<sub>''i''</sub>}} are given by
:<math>[E_i,E_j]=\sum_k{c_{ij}}^kE_k.</math>
The quantities {{math|''c''<sub>''ij''</sub><sup>''k''</sup>}} are the [[structure constant]]s of the Lie algebra (relative to the basis {{math|''E''<sub>''i''</sub>}}).  A simple calculation, using the definition of the exterior derivative {{math|''d''}}, yields
:<math>d\theta^i(E_j,E_k) = -\theta^i([E_j,E_k]) = -\sum_r {c_{jk}}^r\theta^i(E_r) = -{c_{jk}}^i = -\frac{1}{2}({c_{jk}}^i - {c_{kj}}^i),</math>
so that by duality
{{NumBlk|:|<math>d\theta^i=-\frac12 \sum_{jk} {c_{jk}}^i\theta^j\wedge\theta^k.</math>|{{EquationRef|2}}}}
This equation is also often called the '''Maurer&ndash;Cartan equation'''.  To relate it to the previous definition, which only involved the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form {{math|''ω''}}, take the exterior derivative of {{EquationNote|(1)}}:
:<math>d\omega = \sum_i E_i(e)\otimes d\theta^i\,=\,-\frac12 \sum_{ijk}{c_{jk}}^iE_i(e)\otimes\theta^j\wedge\theta^k.</math>
The frame components are given by
:<math>d\omega(E_j,E_k) = -\sum_i {c_{jk}}^iE_i(e) = -[E_j(e),E_k(e)]=-[\omega(E_j),\omega(E_k)],</math>
which establishes the equivalence of the two forms of the Maurer&ndash;Cartan equation.

==On a homogeneous space==
Maurer&ndash;Cartan forms play an important role in Cartan's [[method of moving frames]].  In this context, one may view the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form as a {{nowrap|{{math|1}}-form}} defined on the tautological [[principal bundle]] associated with a [[homogeneous space]].  If {{math|''H''}} is a [[closed subgroup]] of {{math|''G''}}, then {{math|''G''/''H''}} is a smooth manifold of dimension  {{math|dim ''G'' − dim ''H''}}.  The quotient map {{math|''G'' → ''G''/''H''}} induces  the structure of an {{math|''H''}}-principal bundle over {{math|''G''/''H''}}.  The Maurer&ndash;Cartan form on the Lie group {{math|''G''}} yields a flat [[Cartan connection]] for this principal bundle. In particular, if {{math|''H'' {{=}} <nowiki/>{''e''<nowiki/>}}}, then this Cartan connection is an ordinary [[connection form]], and we have
:<math>d\omega+\omega\wedge\omega=0</math>
which is the condition for the vanishing of the curvature.

In the method of moving frames, one sometimes considers a local section of the [[tautological bundle]], say {{math|''s'' : ''G''/''H'' → ''G''}}.  (If working on a [[submanifold]] of the homogeneous space, then {{math|''s''}} need only be a local section over the submanifold.)  The [[pullback (differential geometry)|pullback]] of the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form along {{math|''s''}} defines a non-degenerate {{math|'''g'''}}-valued {{math|1}}-form {{math|''θ'' {{=}} ''s''<sup>*</sup>''ω''}} over the base.  The Maurer&ndash;Cartan equation implies that
:<math>d\theta + \frac{1}{2}[\theta,\theta]=0.</math>

Moreover, if {{math|''s''<sub>''U''</sub>}} and {{math|''s''<sub>''V''</sub>}} are a pair of local sections defined, respectively, over open sets {{math|''U''}} and {{math|''V''}}, then they are related by an element of {{math|''H''}} in each fibre of the bundle:
:<math>h_{UV}(x) = s_V\circ s_U^{-1}(x),\quad x \in U \cap V.</math>
The differential of {{math|''h''}} gives a compatibility condition relating the two sections on the overlap region:
:<math>\theta_V = \operatorname{Ad}(h^{-1}_{UV})\theta_U + (h_{UV})^* \omega_H </math>
where {{math|''ω''<sub>''H''</sub>}} is the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form on the group {{math|''H''}}.

A system of non-degenerate {{math|'''g'''}}-valued {{math|1}}-forms {{math|''θ''<sub>''U''</sub>}} defined on open sets in a manifold {{math|''M''}}, satisfying the Maurer&ndash;Cartan structural equations and the compatibility conditions endows the manifold {{math|''M''}} locally with the structure of the homogeneous space {{math|''G''/''H''}}.  In other words, there is locally a [[diffeomorphism]] of {{math|''M''}} into the homogeneous space, such that {{math|''θ''<sub>''U''</sub>}} is the pullback of the Maurer&ndash;Cartan form along some section of the tautological bundle.  This is a consequence of the existence of primitives of the [[Darboux derivative]].
